div.head: ECf 32 B 13
div.ab: In qua itaque supersint ardua compota et ambigua placita corone et curie domini regis tocius regni predicti; que usus et consuetudines suas una semper inuiolabilitate conseruat, ubicunque ipse rex fuerit, siue in expeditione siue alibi, propter fatigationes gentium et populorum regni, iuxta ueteres consuetudines bonorum patrum et predecessorum et omnium principum et procerum et sapientum seniorum tocius regni predicti.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 657 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 B …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
Liebermann prints the words borrowed from Hn 9, 10a in smaller type; his margin names the source (Hn. 9, 10a).

note.seg: Exchequer und Reichsgerichte sitzen erst seit Richard I. ständig zu Westminster; vgl. Hughes Dial. de scacc. p. 43; Pollock-Maitland HEL. I 148
the Exchequer and the courts of the realm sit permanently at Westminster only from Richard I; cf. Hughes, Dial. de scacc. p. 43; Pollock–Maitland, HEL. I 148
so K; supersunt (geänd. -fuit Or) Or Ld; semper empfiehlt Riley zu Liber albus, was gemäss 32 B 12; aber Hn hat super
so K; supersunt (altered -fuit Or) Or Ld; Riley, on the Liber albus, recommends semper, which accords with 32 B 12; but Hn has super
immobil. seruat ubique Hn; ubique fügt zu K Co L. alb.
immobil. seruat ubique Hn; K Co L. alb. add ubique

div.ab: In it therefore let the difficult accounts and doubtful pleas of the crown and of the court of the lord king of the whole aforesaid kingdom be [?]; and it always keeps its usages and customs with one inviolability, wherever the king himself may be, whether on an expedition or elsewhere, on account of the burdens of the nations and peoples of the kingdom, according to the old customs of the good fathers and predecessors and of all the princes and nobles and wise elders of the whole aforesaid kingdom.

Ibid. Königsgericht 13.a; Reichsrat 1e; propter fatigationes 'to avoid the toils of travel' — supersunt33 — immobilitate seruat35 ubique as Hn, thus the more original reading — constitutiones b. p.37 better Rs
